text:
anya: Quick readiness check — I'm onboarding open-mix-1.2. Weights uploaded to s3://redwood-models/onboard/open-mix-1.2/weights.pt. Can infra/runtime confirm KV cache format & memory sizing before we flip the canary? Also seeing a tokenizer quirk: BOS token seems duplicated when we push beyond 4096 tokens.

mike: Thanks. Couple quick Qs — is the weights file sharded or a single file? Also what's model config: num_layers / hidden_size / max_position_embeddings?

anya: single file, ~5.3GB (fp16). Model config excerpt in repo: max_position_embeddings: 8192, num_hidden_layers: 32, hidden_size: 4096, num_attention_heads: 32.

infra-bot: s3 upload check: permissions OK, object available to redwood-infra role. :white_check_mark:

sara: Re: tokenizer — I dug in; tokenizer.json is missing special_tokens_map and pad_token is null. When we call tokenizer.encode_plus with add_special_tokens it ends up inserting an extra BOS after the prompt for long sequences. Quick workaround: set tokenizer.pad_token = "<pad>" and tokenizer.add_bos = False before batching. I'll open a tiny patch.

thomas: Runtime notes: current KV cache implementation for onboarding expects per-layer serialization (we call it "layer-sharded-fp16"). The runtime stores K and V per layer, contiguous, dtype=fp16. Important for memory calc: for this architecture (32 layers, hidden 4096, 32 heads => head_dim 128) you get ~16KB per layer per token (k+v), so ~512KB per token total across layers. That means: 1 sequence of 8192 tokens => ~4GB KV alone (batch=1). If you bump batch>1 multiply accordingly.

anya: that's super helpful. So for A100-40GB we need headroom for model params (~5.3GB), optimizer/extra (~1GB for profiling), KV (~4GB) — leaves ~29GB free but fragmentation and other buffers matter. Realistically expect OOM if we try batch>2 at 8192.

mike: Good catch. Options: reduce max_context for hosted canary (set to 4096), enable KV sharding across GPUs (requires dedicated nodes), or auto-evict prefix cache for very long sequences. Which is preferred for onboarding?

thomas: For canary, simplest: set max_context to 4096 and confirm tokenizer fixes. If customer needs 8192 we should run on dedicated nodes with KV sharding; runtime flag is `--kv-shard=auto` (requires at least 2 GPUs to be effective). Also can enable `--reserve-mem=0.2` to keep headroom.

anya: I'll update model config in the onboarding repo to `max_position_embeddings: 4096` for the initial canary and open a follow-up to exercise 8192 on dedicated. Pinging @devex for docs update.

devex-bot: PR hint: opened draft PR #3492 to document tokenizer workaround + config recommendations.

sara: Small patch note (snippet):
```python
# onboarding tokenizer fix
tokenizer.pad_token = "<pad>"
tokenizer.special_tokens_map = {"bos_token": "<s>", "eos_token": "</s>", "pad_token": "<pad>"}
# ensure we don't double-add BOS during batching
tokenizer.add_bos = False
```

mike: Also double-check model config key names: runtime validates `max_position_embeddings`, `num_hidden_layers`, `hidden_size`, `num_attention_heads`, and `kv_cache_format`. If kv_cache_format missing it'll default to `layer-sharded-fp16`.

anya: I'll push the config change and run a canary with batch=1 seq=4096 on staging. Will report back with memory profile logs.

thomas: When you run the canary, grab `/metrics/runtime/mem/alloc` and `/traces/kv/cache_size` — that'll give a clear headroom number. If you still see >70% mem on A100-40 we should opt for 4096 prod limit.

anya: Got it. ETA: I'll run canary this afternoon and post results. Thanks all. :pray:
